title: Decompose MaintenanceAgentServices into bounded modules
description:
Problem: MaintenanceAgentServices.cs combines proposal store, workflow, topic map, scheduler, and runtime services in one oversized file.

Desired outcome: improve cohesion and maintainability by splitting maintenance-agent concerns into bounded service files with explicit contracts.

Scope:
- In scope: separate proposal storage/workflow, topic-map logic, scheduler/runtime orchestration, and shared models.
- Out of scope: changes to proposal semantics or scheduler behavior intent.

Dependencies:
- Characterization tests for maintenance workflow and scheduler behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Maintenance hotspot file is materially reduced and responsibilities are modularized.
- Proposal and scheduler behavior remains stable under existing tests.
- New service boundaries are documented in code comments or docs where needed.

Validation:
- Run maintenance-agent and proposals-related test suites.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from F-002 as Sprint 1 committed decomposition work.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Audit #9 (2026-06-11) type inventory to guide the split (file now 2,187 lines): MaintenanceActiveRunStore (37-71), MaintenanceAgentConfigService (217-348), MaintenanceResourceProbe (357-408), MaintenanceDiffService (409-467), MaintenanceWritePermissionService (468-533), IMaintenanceProposalStore + FileMaintenanceProposalStore (534-671), MaintenanceProposalWorkflow (672-942), MaintenanceTopicMapService (967-1263), MaintenanceAgentService (1264-2075), MaintenanceAgentSchedulerService (2076-2187). The proposal cluster (store + workflow) is a genuinely DEEP module - status-transition complexity behind a 5-method seam - and should move as ONE unit. The rest is pure file gravity: mechanical moves, no interface changes. SecurityServices.cs counterpart is TSK-0285. Graded Worth exploring.
